name: Argument Structure Profiling
description: Analyzes the rigidity and telegraphing of discourse transitions and argument frameworks
mechanism: This method evaluates the architectural rigidity of an argument. LLMs are fine-tuned to be extremely structured and readable, which often results in textbook-perfect 'five-paragraph essay' templates. They heavily telegraph their transitions using explicitly predictable discourse markers ('Firstly', 'Furthermore', 'Moreover', 'In conclusion'). Authentic human discourse, especially from experts, is far more organic—humans weave claims together, overlap evidence, defer conclusions, or use implicit logical transitions rather than constantly signposting. By mapping the topological sequence of claims and transitional markers, the system identifies the overly mechanical, predictable scaffolding typical of AI generation.
parameters:
Analysis type: Discourse topology mapping
Media: Text
Input: Formatted/Raw text
Minimum length: 200 words
Output: Structural rigidity score (0-100)
Processing: Transition detection & logic flow mapping
accuracy: High — 78-86%. Specifically powerful against standard LLM prompt outputs ('Write an essay about...').
source: Discourse analysis and syntactic framework mapping.
useCase: Detecting textbook-perfect, highly rigid argumentative essay structures that rely on repetitive transitional signposting to string together claims.
strengths:
• Targets structural RLHF safety and flow alignment
• Detects 'paint-by-numbers' essay generation
• Highly resistant to simple synonym-swapping evasion techniques
limitations:
• Susceptible to human writers forcing rigidly taught essay formats (e.g., TOEFL/IELTS students)
• Not applicable to narrative fiction or poetic texts
• Less reliable on extremely short texts

references.title: Biber, D. et al. (1999). Longman Grammar of Spoken and Written English. Pearson.
